2. Problem Statement

 

2.1 Background

                The Barangay-Wide Tricycle Operator & Driver Association (TODA) Management & Fare Matrix System is proposed for the San Antonio TODA in Pila, Laguna. The project is approved by the Municipal Mayor, while the San Antonio TODA will serve as the primary client and project partner by providing participation, coordination, and relevant driver information. At present, tricycle drivers display their identification and tariff information on their vehicles. However, these materials may become damaged, lost, outdated, or difficult for commuters to verify. In some cases, the applicable tariff may not be visibly displayed inside the tricycle, which can cause uncertainty regarding the correct fare.

                The proposed system will use a QR code assigned to each participating tricycle driver. When scanned, the QR code will provide commuters with approved driver and tricycle information, including the driver’s name, tricycle number, TODA association, verification status, vehicle plate number, and driver photograph. It will also display the official fare matrix and provide access to a passenger feedback form. The system is intended to improve commuter trust, support driver identification, promote fare transparency, and provide commuters with a convenient channel for submitting comments or concerns. The system will initially support fewer than 25 tricycle drivers serving local residents, students, senior citizens, workers, tourists, and other members of the general public.

 

2.2 Current Challenges

 

1.     Difficulty Identifying Drivers: Commuters may have difficulty confirming the identity of a tricycle driver based only on the physical identification and tariff materials displayed on the vehicle.

2.     Limited Verification of Driver Registration: There is no convenient digital method for commuters to confirm whether a driver is registered with or recognized by the San Antonio TODA and the municipal authorities.

3.     Fare Confusion: Tariff information may not always be clearly visible inside or on the tricycle, making it difficult for commuters to confirm the applicable official fare before or during a trip.

4.     Overcharging Concerns: When fare information is unavailable or unclear, commuters may have difficulty determining whether the amount charged is consistent with the official fare matrix.

5.     Lack of a Convenient Feedback Channel: Commuters currently do not have an established and convenient digital means of submitting feedback, complaints, or commendations regarding their transportation experience.

6.     Manual Record Keeping: Driver information is maintained through municipal records and records managed by the TODA president. This may make information retrieval, updating, and verification more dependent on manual coordination.

7.     Outdated Driver Information: Changes to driver, tricycle, or registration details may not be immediately reflected in the identification materials displayed on the vehicle.

8.     Lost or Damaged Identification Materials: Physical identification cards, stickers, or tariff displays may be lost or damaged, potentially limiting the commuter’s ability to identify the driver or verify fare information.

9.     Limited Access During Travel: Commuters may need access to driver and fare information even when mobile Internet connectivity is unavailable during a journey. A system that requires continuous Internet access may therefore be inconvenient in areas with weak or interrupted connectivity.

10.   Separate Access to Information and Feedback: Driver information, fare details, and passenger feedback may not be available through one organized access point. This can make it more difficult for commuters to find the appropriate information or submit a concern.

 

2.3 Problem Statement

                The San Antonio TODA in Pila, Laguna currently relies primarily on physical driver identification and tariff displays, together with municipal and TODA records, to provide driver and fare information to commuters. However, physical materials may be unclear, outdated, lost, or damaged, while tariff information may not always be visible. In addition, commuters do not have a convenient and organized feedback channel for submitting concerns regarding their transportation experience. The absence of a QR-accessible system may result in difficulty identifying drivers, verifying registration information, confirming official fares, and submitting feedback. These limitations may affect commuter trust, passenger safety, fare transparency, and the ability of the San Antonio TODA and municipal authorities to receive commuter concerns.

               

                Therefore, there is a need for a Barangay-Wide Tricycle Operator & Driver Association (TODA) Management & Fare Matrix System that provides QR-based access to approved driver and tricycle information, displays the official fare matrix, and offers a digital feedback form for commuters. The system should allow public driver and fare information to remain accessible after the initial online visit through browser caching, while requiring an Internet connection when commuters submit feedback through the online form. Driver information will be encoded by the development team based on records and details provided or verified by authorized municipal personnel or the San Antonio TODA president. Feedback may be submitted anonymously, with an optional field for the commuter’s name.

3.2 Out of Scope

#

Excluded Feature

Reason

1

Driver Self-Registration

Driver records will be based on the official municipal list. Drivers will not directly create or update their own profiles through the system.

2

Online Driver Record Management

The system will not provide an administrator dashboard for adding, editing, deleting, or approving driver records.

3

Automated Municipal Approval Workflow

The system will not include a digital workflow for the mayor, municipal personnel, or TODA president to approve or reject driver information within the application.

4

User Account and Login System

The current version will not require commuter accounts, driver accounts, TODA accounts, or administrator login credentials.

5

Mobile Application

The system will be developed as a web-based system and will not include a separate Android or iOS application.

6

Offline Operation

The system will require an Internet connection when the QR code is opened and when the commuter accesses the online content. Offline viewing is not included in the current scope.

7

Payment Processing

The system will not process fare payments, digital wallets, online transactions, or cashless payments.

8

SMS Notifications

The system will not send SMS alerts or text-message notifications to drivers, commuters, the TODA president, or municipal personnel.

9

Automated Email Notifications

The system will not automatically send email alerts for new feedback, complaints, or changes in driver information.

10

Multi-Barangay Support

The current version will cover only one barangay and will not manage drivers from multiple barangays or multiple TODA associations.

11

Real-Time GPS Tracking

The system will not track the live location, route, or movement of tricycles or commuters.

12

Online Booking or Dispatching

The system will not include ride booking, passenger matching, trip scheduling, or vehicle dispatching.

13

Automated Driver Data Synchronization

The system will not automatically synchronize with the municipal records. Driver information will be manually encoded by the development team based on the official records provided.

14

Advanced Reports and Analytics

The system will not provide automated dashboards, statistical charts, or advanced analytics. Feedback responses will be monitored through Google Forms, Google Sheets, or exported CSV files.

15

Complaint Resolution Workflow

The system will collect feedback but will not include case assignment, complaint investigation, resolution tracking, or formal appeals management.

16

Public Editing of Information

Commuters and drivers will not be allowed to directly modify driver information, fare details, photographs, or verification status.

17

Multiple Fare Zones or Dynamic Fare Calculation

The system will display the approved fare matrix but will not calculate fares based on GPS distance, route, traffic, time, or changing conditions.

 

 

3.3 Project Boundaries

            The system is limited to a commuter-facing web application for the San Antonio TODA in Pila, Laguna. Its primary purpose is to provide public access to approved driver information, the official fare matrix, and an online feedback form through assigned QR codes. The system will not replace the official municipal records or the administrative functions of the San Antonio TODA. Instead, it will present selected information from the official records in a more accessible digital format. The development team will encode the driver data, tariff information, municipal approval information, and driver photographs provided by authorized representatives. The system requires an Internet connection to access the deployed website and submit feedback. Google Forms responses will be monitored by the San Antonio TODA president. The current version will not provide an administrative dashboard, user login, mobile application, automatic record synchronization, or offline functionality.

 

The system will use:

·         GitHub Pages under a project-owned GitHub organization

·         Google Forms for commuter feedback

·         Google Sheets or CSV files for response monitoring

·         Assigned QR codes for driver access

 

The initial implementation will cover:

Location: San Antonio, Pila, Laguna

Primary client/supporting organization: San Antonio TODA

Coverage: One Barangay

Number of drivers: Fewer than 25

Primary users: Commuters

System stage: Academic Project

5. Current Process/System

5.1 Current Workflow

Step 1: Commuter boards a tricycle in the barangay

Step 2: Commuter has no way to verify the driver's identity or franchise status

Step 3: Commuter asks the driver verbally for the fare

Step 4: Driver quotes a fare (may differ from the official fare matrix)

Step 5: Commuter pays the quoted fare, or negotiates

Step 6: If there is a problem, commuter must go to the TODA office / barangay hall to complain

Step 7: TODA officer records the complaint in a logbook / notebook

Step 8: TODA President compiles driver records and complaints manually

5

7

8

Commuters in areas with weak signal can't check anything

The system should begin loading the assigned driver page immediately after the QR-code link is opened.

High

NFR-PER-003

Lightweight Resources

The system shall use appropriately sized images, stylesheets, scripts, and other resources to support access through mobile devices.

High

NFR-PER-004

Small Dataset Support

The system shall support the initial dataset of fewer than 25 participating tricycle drivers without noticeable performance problems.

High

NFR-PER-005

Fare Display Performance

The system shall display the fare matrix without requiring a separate page or unnecessary additional processing.

Medium

NFR-PER-006

Feedback Access

The system shall provide access to the external Google Forms feedback page when an Internet connection is available.

High

NFR-PER-007

No Unnecessary Background Processing

The system shall not perform unnecessary continuous background processing, location tracking, or data collection while the commuter views the page.

High

Req ID

Requirement

Description

Priority

Public Information Limitation

High

Sensitive Information Protection

High

High

Optional Personal Information

HTTPS Access

External Form Protection

Public Repository Awareness

Requirement

Description

Priority

9. Security Requirements

 9.1 Confidentiality

Req ID

Requirement

Description

SEC-CONF-01

Limited Public Data

The app shall contain only the driver's name, body number, TODA association, and franchise status

SEC-CONF-02

Private Records

Contact numbers, addresses, and clearance documents shall never be placed in the app or the public repository

SEC-CONF-03

Driver Consent

A driver's details shall be published only with the driver's consent (Data Privacy Act of 2012)

SEC-CONF-04

Restricted Deployment Access

Only authorized maintainers shall have write access to the repository, protected by 2-step verification

SEC-CONF-05

Feedback Access

The Google Sheet of responses shall be shared only with the TODA President and designated officers

SEC-CONF-06

Anonymous Feedback

The Google Form shall not require a name, contact details, or sign-in

SEC-CONF-07

Secure Transport

The app shall be served over HTTPS (enforced by GitHub Pages)

SEC-CONF-08

QR Content

QR codes shall contain only the app URL and a driver ID (?driver=TRIKE-102)

 

9.2 Integrity

Req ID

Requirement

Description

SEC-INTG-01

Unique Driver IDs

Each driver ID shall be unique, and each QR code shall point to exactly one driver

SEC-INTG-02

Unknown ID Handling

An unrecognized driver ID shall show "Driver not found" and no driver details

SEC-INTG-03

Status Display

The franchise status shall always be displayed, and any status other than "Verified" shall be visibly highlighted

SEC-INTG-04

Data Check Before Deploy

Driver and fare data shall be checked for required fields and typos before every update

SEC-INTG-05

Version History

Every change shall be tracked through Git commit history

SEC-INTG-06

Fare Versioning

The fare matrix shall display its version and effective date

SEC-INTG-07

Fare Approval

Fare changes shall be made only after TODA officers approve them

SEC-INTG-08

Feedback Validation

The Google Form shall mark required fields and use dropdowns for categories

 

9.3 Availability

Req ID

Requirement

Description

SEC-AVAIL-01

Offline Viewing

A service worker shall cache the app so driver info and fares load without internet after the first visit

SEC-AVAIL-02

Fresh Data When Online

The service worker shall fetch the newest files first and use the cache only when offline

SEC-AVAIL-03

Online-Only Feedback

When offline, the Feedback button shall show "Internet is required to submit feedback"

SEC-AVAIL-04

Connection Indicator

The app shall show "Internet available" or "Offline mode"

SEC-AVAIL-05

Free Hosting

The system shall be hosted on GitHub Pages

SEC-AVAIL-06

Browser Compatibility

The system shall work in current mobile browsers without installation

SEC-AVAIL-07

Backup

The repository copy and the downloadable Google Sheet shall serve as backups

SEC-AVAIL-08

Data Preservation

Drivers who leave shall be marked inactive instead of deleted

 10.1 General UI Requirements

Req ID

Requirement

Description

UI-01

Single-Page Web App

The system shall be a single-page HTML/CSS/JavaScript app with offline support

UI-02

Mobile-First Layout

The layout shall switch to a single column on screens 600px wide or smaller

Readable Design

The system shall use clear section headings, readable text sizes, and high-contrast colors

UI-04

Language

The interface shall be in English

Section Layout

The page shall present Driver Information, Fare Matrix, and Feedback in that order

Connection Status

A status badge shall show online (green) or offline (amber)

UI-07

Error Feedback

The system shall show clear messages for an unknown driver ID and for feedback attempted offline

UI-08

External Form

The feedback form shall open in a new tab

View

Description

System title and connection status badge

UI-V-02

Driver name, body number, TODA association, and franchise status

Fare Matrix

Version, effective date, and a table of route, regular fare, and special fare

UI-V-04

Feedback

Explanatory text and an "Open Feedback Form" button linking to the Google Form

Unknown Driver State

"Driver not found" message when the QR contains an invalid ID

Offline badge, with cached driver and fare data still shown

Requirement

Description

Encodes only the app URL with the driver ID

Sticker Labels

High error correction so the code scans when scratched or dirty

Optimized for sticker or laminated printing

 

11. System Constraints

#

Constraint

Description

SC-01

Static Hosting Only

The system runs on GitHub Pages with no server-side code, database, or login system

SC-02

Internet for First Load

The app needs an internet connection on the first visit so the service worker can cache it

SC-03

Online-Only Feedback

Feedback submission needs internet because it depends on Google Forms

SC-04

Public Data

Free GitHub Pages needs a public repository, so all driver and fare data in the app is publicly readable

SC-05

Hardcoded Data

Driver and fare data are stored in index.html, so every update requires editing the file and redeploying

SC-06

Google Dependency

Feedback collection depends on Google Forms and Google Sheets staying free and available

SC-07

No Authentication

The commuter app has no accounts, and there is no in-app admin panel

SC-08

Browser Requirement

Must use a modern browser with service worker support (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) over HTTPS

SC-09

No Native Mobile App

The system is accessed only through the browser after a QR scan

SC-10

Single Barangay

The system is designed for one barangay's TODA drivers

SC-11

Data Volume

The system is optimized for up to about 100 driver records, because all data loads in one page

SC-12

Language

The interface and data are in English only

SC-13

Hosting Limits

GitHub Pages has soft limits on site size (about 1 GB) and monthly bandwidth

SC-14

No Automated Backup

Backup relies on the repository copy and a manual download of the Google Sheet

 

12. System Assumptions

#

Assumption

SA-01

Commuters have a smartphone with a camera or QR scanner and a modern browser

SA-02

Commuters have internet at least once to open the system and cache it

SA-03

Internet connectivity may be unavailable or unreliable while riding

SA-04

At least one TODA member will be designated as the system maintainer

SA-05

The maintainer has basic skills in editing HTML files and using GitHub

SA-06

TODA officers will provide the verified list of drivers and body numbers

SA-07

Each driver gives consent before their details are published

SA-08

TODA officers will approve the fare matrix before it is published

SA-09

Fare changes are infrequent (for example, once or twice a year)

SA-10

QR stickers will be printed and attached to each tricycle by the TODA

SA-11

The Google Form and Sheet are owned by the TODA President's account, with access shared only with designated officers

SA-12

GitHub Pages and Google Forms will remain free and available

SA-13

Drivers' franchise status is checked and updated regularly by TODA officers

SA-14

Commuters who need help using the system can ask the driver or a TODA officer

SA-15

Data is entered in English or Filipino names, and no multi-language support is required

SA-16

The prototype is intended for academic presentation and may be extended later

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

13. Requirement Priorities

 Requirements are classified using the following priority levels:

Priority

Definition

P1 - Critical

Must be implemented for the system to be functional. The system cannot go live without these.

P2 - High

Essential for core workflows. Significant impact on usability if omitted.

P3 - Medium

Important for completeness and user satisfaction. Can be deferred to a later phase.

P4 - Low

Nice-to-have features. Minimal impact on core functionality if omitted.

 

Priority Distribution

Priority

Count

Examples

P1 - Critical

20

QR scan access, driver info display, fare matrix display, offline viewing, unique driver IDs, HTTPS, limited public data

P2 - High

21

Feedback form button, readable design, error messages, fare approval, restricted deployment access, free hosting

P3 - Medium

18

Connection status badge, fare versioning, Git version history, Google Sheets feedback view, fresh data when online

P4 - Low

2

Soft-delete of inactive drivers, print layout optimization for stickers

15. Requirement Validation

 Requirements are classified using the following priority levels:

15.1 Validation Criteria

#

Criterion

Description

V-01

Completeness

Each requirement is fully stated without ambiguity.

V-02

Consistency

No requirement conflicts with another requirement.

V-03

Feasibility

Each requirement can be implemented within project constraints.

V-04

Testability

Each requirement has at least one verifiable test case.

V-05

Traceability

Each requirement can be traced to a stakeholder need.

 

15.2 Validation Methods

Method

Applicable Requirements

Description

Code Review

All FR, NFR

Review implementation against requirement specification.

Functional Testing

FR-QR, FR-DRV, FR-FAR, FR-FBK, FR-CON, FR-DAT, FR-MON

Execute test cases for each functional module.

Performance Testing

NFR-PER-001 through NFR-PER-007

Measure response times, concurrent users, and cache behavior.

Security Testing

NFR-SEC-001 through NFR-SEC-010

Attempt unauthorized access, injection attacks, and data corruption.

Usability Testing

NFR-USE-001 through NFR-USE-009, NFR-ACC-001 through NFR-ACC-006

User acceptance testing with actual commuters and TODA officials.

Compatibility Testing

NFR-CMP-001 through NFR-CMP-007

Test on Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Offline Testing

NFR-AVL-001 through NFR-AVL-007

Disconnect from the Internet and verify that features work when appropriate.

Backup/Recovery Testing

NFR-MNT-005, NFR-MNT-006, NFR-DEP-006, NFR-DAT-008

Perform backup and restore cycle, verify data integrity.
